title: Program-level cleanup of horizontal duplication and orphan code found by the 2026-10-27 codebase simplification audit
goal: The 2026-10-27 read-only audit (docs/reviews/CODEBASE_SIMPLIFICATION_AUDIT.md) found the repository architecturally healthy but carrying horizontal duplication debt: the same tenant-scope trio is re-implemented in about 11 services, pagination normalization exists in about 13 copies, path-ID parsing is inlined about 35 times, import/export boilerplate is repeated across 8 modules, and 11 handler files redeclare the same two error values. It also found a small set of genuinely dead code, the largest being the 129-line zero-caller pkg/common/token.go pass-through layer. This program converts the audit's three-batch plan into twelve independently reviewable waves: batch S1 removes dead code and narrows over-exported symbols, batch S2 converges the shared handler and service helpers behind tests, and batch S3 touches tenant scoping, the role data-scope model, the OIDC response envelope and maintainer-only governance decisions. No wave changes routes, permission codes, menus, i18n keys, error envelopes, database schema or migrations; every wave must keep go test ./backend/... at 46 ok / 0 FAIL and keep the existing gates green.
findings: AUDIT-001 / RC-001 (P1): backend/pkg/common/token.go is a 129-line, 34-export pass-through to pkg/authtoken and pkg/common/http with zero callers anywhere in the repo or in the pantheon-ops business overlay.

AUDIT-002 / RC-012 (P1): the tenant-scope trio (WithTenantContext / scoped / tenantOwnerID) is duplicated in about 11 services (role, post, dept, user, dict, setting, permission, dashboard, login, security, session).
AUDIT-003 / RC-013 (P1): pagination normalization is re-implemented about 13 times, including two copies inside role_helper.go, and Offset((page-1)*pageSize).Limit(pageSize) appears about 14 times.
AUDIT-004 / RC-014 (P1): strconv.ParseUint(c.Param("id"), 10, 64) plus a 400 response block is inlined about 35 times; only user_handler.go extracted parseUintParam.
AUDIT-005 / RC-016 (P1): import / export / template-download boilerplate repeats across about 8 modules; RC-015 adds 6-8 sort-whitelist helper copies.
AUDIT-006 / RC-017 (P1): errParamInvalid and errRequestFailed are redeclared in 11 handler files.
AUDIT-007 / RC-019 (P1): the common package duplicates itself and the modules keep a third copy (GetUserID, IsI18nMessageKey, ResolveErrorMessageKey, getRoleKeysFromContext, getUserIDFromContext).

AUDIT-008 / RC-002, RC-003, RC-005, RC-007, RC-029 (P2): dead or over-exported symbols: StructuredLoggingMiddleware, common.ErrorResponse, database.SetEx, rbacbind singular insert helpers, permissionServiceErrorCode pass-through.
AUDIT-009 / RC-010, RC-011 (P2): 13 orphan frontend scripts (10 capture-*.mjs plus 3 one-off tools) are referenced by no package.json script, CI workflow or other script.

AUDIT-010 / RC-036, RC-037, RC-038 (P2): governance surface exceeds product surface; 99 unvalidated .en.md copies, 6-7 unindexed LLM review transcripts and 659 archive files need a maintainer disposition rather than an agent decision.

in: Wave S1: delete zero-caller code and narrow over-exported symbols (RC-001 to RC-005, RC-007, RC-009 to RC-011, RC-029)

Wave S2: add shared helpers with tests, then migrate call sites for ID parsing, pagination, sorting, not-found handling, batch actions and import/export (RC-013 to RC-019, RC-023, RC-024, RC-028, RC-030)
Wave S3: unify tenant scoping, review the mirrored role data-scope model, normalise the OIDC envelope and record maintainer decisions (RC-012, RC-022, RC-026, RC-027, RC-031, RC-036, RC-037, RC-043)
Per-wave evidence under .harness/evidence/<wave-task-id>/ with commands.json, summary.md and review.md
Foundation release + base -> ops sync check after every merged wave
out: Any behavioural change: routes, request/response shapes, error codes, i18n keys, permission codes, menus and seeds stay byte-identical
Database schema, migrations, backfills or data repair of any kind
Dependency upgrades or new dependencies, including dev tooling
Deleting tests or weakening assertions to make a refactor pass
Reducing the exported surface of frontend/src/index.ts, which is the only stable downstream contract
Merging the dept and post modules, or genericising the seven handler service wrappers (explicitly rejected in the audit)
Touching pantheon-ops business code; only compatibility verification is in scope

implementationNotes: Every wave is a separate task packet with its own manifest, evidence directory and review; waves may be reordered inside a batch but not across batches.
Batch S1 must land and be released before batch S2 starts; batch S2 must be stable for one release cycle before batch S3 is scheduled.

Convergence means one implementation of how a thing is done, never one value of what it is: column whitelists, page-size caps, i18n keys and module-specific error codes stay per module and are passed in as parameters.
If a shared helper needs a third optional parameter to fit one more module, stop and keep that module's local implementation; record the exception in the wave review instead of growing the helper.
One pattern per commit. Do not mix pagination migration and error-mapping migration in one commit, so git bisect stays useful.
The planner/dispatcher must not edit backend/ or frontend/src/; each wave must be executed by the Generator adapter and the handoff recorded in the task packet and evidence.
Refusals only where behaviour could change: if a wave cannot prove equivalence, the wave closes as abandoned with the reason, not as completed.

doNotTouch: the published tags and release assets

executionRoles.implementerPosture: Execute one wave per task packet through the Generator adapter; each wave is independently reviewable, independently revertable and proves equivalence before merge.
reviewerPosture: Verify the wave removed duplication rather than behaviour: diff response envelopes, error codes, i18n keys and permission checks.
Reject any wave whose diff touches routing, migrations, permission codes, menus or seeds.
Reject any wave that edits or deletes a test to make a refactor pass.
Confirm the shared helper did not absorb module-specific values through extra optional parameters.
Confirm the wave reports its measured diff stat instead of the audit's estimate.
Confirm pantheon-ops still builds after the foundation release sync.

runtimeEvidence: go test package count and pass/fail totals before and after each wave (baseline: 46 ok, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP)
git diff --stat per wave, compared with the audit estimate and recorded as the measured gain
for any wave that touches an HTTP response path: a before/after response body snapshot for one affected endpoint
